ety.text: Clipped compound of авиацио́нный бензи́н (aviaciónnyj benzín). By surface analysis, авиа- (avia-) + бензи́н (benzín). Compare Ukrainian авіабензи́н (aviabenzýn).

x: Он заме́тил, что деви́цу по безмо́лвному соглаше́нию вы́черкнули из о́бщего разгово́ра.

ety.text: Borrowed from Old Church Slavonic безмлъвьнъ (bezmlŭvĭnŭ). By surface analysis, без- (bez-) + молва́ (molvá) + -ный (-nyj)

s.g: blockbuster (film or book, that sustains exceptional and widespread popularity and achieves enormous sales)
Hesiod (an ancient Greek epic poet and rhapsodist of the 8th century BCE, known as the first author of didactic verse)
hydride (a compound of hydrogen with a more electropositive element)

x: – Со́рок мину́т не разгова́ривали? – усмехну́лся Серге́й. – В гляде́лки игра́ли?

s.g: a direction whence a wet and cold wind comes, bringing fog and bad weather. This direction depends on the geolocation (e.g. on the Commander Islands it is the south-west, while in northern European Russia it is the north-west)
to guess (to reach an unqualified conclusion)
to surmise, to suspect, to conjecture
to cotton on, to glom on
horsecar, a tram drawn by horses

ety.text: Borrowed from Dutch lijf (“corsage”). Doublet of лейб- (lejb-).

x: Мно́гие говоря́т, что ско́ро бу́дет война́.
ибо многие придут под именем Моим и будут говорить, что это Я; и многих прельстят.

s.g: to come unexpectedly (out of the blue)

ety.text: Borrowed from Spanish ñandú, of Paraguayan Guarani origin.

s.g: in a valid, well-founded, justified manner
x: Клубни́ку счита́ют, и не без основа́ния, лу́чшей из я́год.

s.g: well, well then, right (in the sense of marking a transition to a new thought, action or summary, as if pronounced – in either English or Russian – ending with a falling tone and a subsequent pausa)
x: Ну что ж, пора́ нам идти́.

ety.text: перемыка́ть (peremykátʹ) + -ка (-ka). Compare Polish przesmyk (akin to пресмыка́ться (presmykátʹsja)).

s.g: acronym of Па́ртия жу́ликов и воро́в (Pártija žúlikov i voróv): Party of crooks and thieves (sarcastic reference to the United Russia party of Vladimir Putin)
obedient, dutiful, amenable, agreeable (willing to comply with)

ety.text: послу́шать (poslúšatʹ) + -ный (-nyj) Compare typologically Latin oboediēns (whence English obedient) (<< audiō), Ancient Greek ὑπήκοος (hupḗkoos) (<< ἀκούω (akoúō)), Dutch gehoorzaam (<< horen).

s.g: to be allowed, to be permitted

Transnistria (a geographic region and de-facto independent but unrecognized country in Eastern Europe that claims statehood as the Pridnestrovian Moldavian Republic; internationally considered an autonomous territorial unit within Moldova)
to be dreamed [with dative ‘by someone’] (idiomatically translated by English dream with the dative object as the subject)
for one to dream [with dative ‘by someone’ and что (što) ‘that ...’] (idiomatically translated by English dream with the dative object as the subject)

ety.text: From при- (pri-) + сни́ться (snítʹsja). Compare Czech přisnít, Kashubian przësnic, Silesian prziśnić, and Polish przyśnić.

s.g: apiary (a place where bees and hives are kept)

ety.text: Inherited from Old East Slavic *бьчельникъ (*bĭčelĭnikŭ), from Proto-Slavic *bьčelьnikъ. By surface analysis, пчела́ (pčelá) + -ник (-nik).

s.g: to deliver, to transport (multiple people or things to their respective destinations)
diversity, variety (quality of being diverse; difference)
one who has not stained himself with unworthy, vile or immoral acts, someone you can shake hands with
a surname, Senkevich, from Belarusian, equivalent to Belarusian Сянке́віч (Sjankjévič)
a surname from Polish, equivalent to Polish Sienkiewicz

ety.text: Borrowed from Japanese 島根 (しまね, Shimane).
Per Dal, from стыка́ть (stykátʹ, “to connect, to join”) + -ка (-ka); presumably the sense development was "joining" → "meeting" → "skirmishing".

s.g: garrote, any kind of choking weapon
to entreat, to beg, to beseech, to prevail (upon)

ety.text: Borrowed from Latin fīcus (“fig”), likely via Polish figa, from Middle High German vîge, from Old High German fîga.
